workshopTitle: Google Antigravity workshop by T M Saravanan

prompts.title: Prompt 1: Website Header & Intro
prompts.content:
Act as a creative UI/UX designer and frontend engineer. Using Antigravity IDE, create the top navigation bar and opening 'Hero' intro screen for my student developer portfolio using React and Tailwind CSS.

* Theme & Style: 'Cyber-Emerald / Dark Mode' (avoid common blue gradients). Use a deep matte carbon background (#0d1117) with crisp neon emerald (#10b981) and bright lime accents.
* Background Effect: A subtle animated matrix-dot grid on an HTML5 canvas that gently shifts perspective or ripples when the mouse moves over it.
* Navigation Bar: A floating frosted-glass navbar at the top that stays fixed as I scroll, with my name/logo and clean links: 'About', 'Projects', 'Skills', 'Campus Life', and 'Contact'.
* Intro Section Content:
* Status Badge: An animated blinking radar pill: '🟢 Student Developer // Open for Internships'
* Main Headline: 'Hey, I am [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] — Building the Future of Tech.'
* Student Bio: '[REPLACE: YOUR DEGREE & COLLEGE, e.g., 2nd Year Computer Science Student at XYZ University] passionate about web development, AI, and building real-world projects.'
* Action Buttons: A glowing emerald primary button 'View My Projects' that lifts slightly on hover, and an outline secondary button 'Download Resume / CV'.

* Ensure the layout is fully responsive and looks great on both laptop and mobile screens.
prompts.notes: Swap [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] with your name and [REPLACE: YOUR DEGREE & COLLEGE] with your branch and year. Leave the color codes like #0d1117 as they are so the dark theme stays clean.
prompts.presenterTip: Swap [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] with your name and [REPLACE: YOUR DEGREE & COLLEGE] with your branch and year. Leave the color codes like #0d1117 as they are so the dark theme stays clean.
prompts.whyItWorks: Establishes an exact visual theme, color palette, and clear visual hierarchy (status badge, headline, student bio, dual buttons) so the coding agent outputs clean code instead of unstructured blocks.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Build me a hero section for my student portfolio with cool green colors and my name Alex.'
Why it fails: "Cool green colors" is subjective and usually produces unreadable bright lime text on white backgrounds, broken button margins, and no mobile-responsive design.

prompts.title: Prompt 2: Project Cards
prompts.content:
Keep the existing dark carbon and emerald theme intact. Directly below the intro section, add a 'Featured Projects' showcase.

* Layout: A clean, responsive 3-column grid featuring 3 student project cards.
* Interactive Card Physics:
* Style cards like dark glass panels with a thin border (border-emerald-500/20).
* Add an interactive 3D perspective tilt effect where the card tilts subtly based on mouse cursor position.
* On hover: The card should lift up smoothly (translateY(-6px)), cast a soft emerald glow around its edges, and reveal a sleek shine effect.

* Card Content:
* Project 1: [REPLACE: Project 1 Title, e.g., Campus Event Finder] — A 2-sentence description of what it solves, tech badges (e.g., 'React', 'Firebase'), and two clickable buttons: 'Live Demo' and 'GitHub Code'.
* Project 2: [REPLACE: Project 2 Title, e.g., Smart Attendance Tracker] — A 2-sentence description and tech badges (e.g., 'Python', 'OpenCV').
* Project 3: [REPLACE: Project 3 Title, e.g., Student Notes Marketplace] — A 2-sentence description and tech badges (e.g., 'Tailwind', 'Node.js').

* Add a filter pill row above the grid ('All', 'Web Apps', 'AI / ML', 'Mini-Projects') that smoothly filters the items.
prompts.notes: Fill in real titles for class or hackathon projects. If you don't have three finished yet, use placeholders like 'Smart Timetable App' or 'Campus Food Delivery' to keep moving forward.
prompts.presenterTip: Fill in real titles for class or hackathon projects. If you don't have three finished yet, use placeholders like 'Smart Timetable App' or 'Campus Food Delivery' to keep moving forward.
prompts.whyItWorks: Maintains design continuity with previous sections, defines uniform card data, and uses precise movement parameters (translateY(-6px)) to avoid glitchy animations.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Put 3 projects on the page and make the cards move when I put my mouse on them.'
Why it fails: Lacks data structure and motion boundaries, causing the AI to write jittery mouse-tracking scripts that break scrolling and card alignment.

prompts.title: Prompt 3: Technical Skills
prompts.content:
Add an interactive 'Tech Stack & Skills' section directly below the projects, matching our cyber-emerald style.

* Categorized Skill Layout: Group my skills into 3 tidy categories: 'Languages' (e.g., C++, Python, JavaScript, Java), 'Frameworks & Tools' (e.g., React, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Git/GitHub), and 'Core CS Concepts' (e.g., Data Structures, OOP, DBMS, OS).
* Interactive Pill Badges:
* Render each skill as a sleek badge with its small official tech logo/icon.
* When hovering over any skill badge, make it scale up slightly (scale-105), glow with an emerald border, and display a tiny tooltip indicating my comfort level (e.g., 'Proficient', 'Familiar', or 'Currently Learning').

* Keep the design clean, lightweight, and modern without clutter.
prompts.notes: Update the skills list with languages you actually study in college or on your own. Hover over the badges to make sure the tooltip and scale effects appear.
prompts.presenterTip: Update the skills list with languages you actually study in college or on your own. Hover over the badges to make sure the tooltip and scale effects appear.
prompts.whyItWorks: Organizes skills specifically for student recruiters by separating core CS fundamentals from practical frameworks, adding transparent proficiency tags (Currently Learning).
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'List out all my programming skills with icons.'
Why it fails: Dumps an unorganized wall of icons with no distinction between frontend, backend, or college syllabus topics.

prompts.title: Prompt 4: Campus Life & Achievements
prompts.content:
Add an engaging 'Education & Campus Journey' section below the skills to highlight my college background and student activities.

* Interactive Milestone Timeline:
* Build a clean vertical timeline connected by an illuminated emerald line with glowing nodal dots.
* 3 Milestones:
* 2026: [REPLACE: Current Milestone, e.g., Pre-Final Year B.Tech & Hackathon Finalist] — Brief 1-line note.
* 2025: [REPLACE: Past Milestone, e.g., Core Technical Club Member / Web Lead] — Brief 1-line note.
* 2024: [REPLACE: Starting Milestone, e.g., Began Degree & Built First Web App] — Brief 1-line note.

* Achievement Badges:
* Next to or below the timeline, add a compact 2x2 grid of accomplishment callouts (e.g., '🏆 1st Place - University Hackathon', '⚡ 150+ LeetCode Problems Solved', '👥 Tech Club Organizer', '📜 Full-Stack Certified').
* Each badge should have a subtle hover highlight.
prompts.notes: Fill in your real club roles, coding problem milestones, or hackathon participations. If a date is different from your graduation schedule, update the years directly in the brackets.
prompts.presenterTip: Fill in your real club roles, coding problem milestones, or hackathon participations. If a date is different from your graduation schedule, update the years directly in the brackets.
prompts.whyItWorks: Builds a timeline suited for college students who have club activities, hackathons, and certifications instead of formal 10-year corporate career histories.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Add a work experience timeline for my college stuff and some achievements.'
Why it fails: The AI defaults to senior enterprise roles and generates corporate placeholder text like 'Senior Director at Tech Corp'.

prompts.title: Prompt 5: Contact Form & Final Effects
prompts.content:
Finish the entire portfolio by adding a student-friendly 'Get In Touch' section, interactive background polish, and a clean footer.

* Contact Card:
* Headline: 'Let’s Collaborate & Build'
* Subtitle: 'Open for summer internships, open-source projects, or tech chats. Drop me a message!'
* Interactive Form: Clean input fields for 'Your Name', 'Your Email', and 'Your Message'.
* Submit Button: 'Send Message'. When clicked, animate the button to show an emerald loading spinner and change the text to 'Message Sent! 🚀' as feedback.
* Direct Links: Sleek icon buttons with a magnetic hover effect for GitHub, LinkedIn, and Email ([REPLACE: your.email@example.com]).

* Interactive Mouse Feature (Easter Egg):
* Add a subtle custom cursor follower or gentle trailing light spark that smoothly tracks the user's mouse position across the screen.

* Footer:
* Centered line: 'Designed & Engineered by [REPLACE: YOUR NAME] • Class of [REPLACE: YOUR GRADUATION YEAR, e.g., 2027].'

* Deliver the full, unified, production-ready code with all styles and scripts so it compiles without errors in Antigravity IDE.
prompts.notes: Add your real email, LinkedIn profile, and graduation year. Once Antigravity completes the generation, move your mouse around to test the cursor trail and click the submit button to test the sent-message animation.
prompts.presenterTip: Add your real email, LinkedIn profile, and graduation year. Once Antigravity completes the generation, move your mouse around to test the cursor trail and click the submit button to test the sent-message animation.
prompts.whyItWorks: Provides student-appropriate outreach copy, demonstrates live UI feedback states (Message Sent! 🚀), and requests a single unified deliverable to avoid runtime errors.
prompts.howNotToPrompt:
Example: 'Finish the page with a contact form and a cool mouse effect and footer.'
Why it fails: Replacing the native cursor blindly often disables mouse clicks entirely, making links and buttons unclickable.
